content: 1. Data on the safety and efficacy of switching chronic hepatitis B patients with risk factors for tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) has been published, highlighting outcomes in virologically suppressed individuals. (Gastroenterology, 2018) 2. A randomized, double-blind, phase 3 multicenter study demonstrated that switching from TDF to TAF in virologically suppressed chronic hepatitis B patients maintained non-inferiority in terms of efficacy and safety. (Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol, 2020) 3. A 96-week comparative study of TAF versus TDF for hepatitis B virus infection showed that TAF was effective and associated with improved safety profiles, particularly in terms of renal and bone health. (J Hepatol, 2018) 4. Research has shown that tenofovir use is associated with a higher risk of kidney function decline compared to entecavir in patients with chronic hepatitis B. (Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol) 5. Excess weight gain observed with integrase inhibitors and TAF has raised questions about the underlying mechanisms and clinical significance of this phenomenon. (Open Forum Infect Dis, 2021) 6. A review of current data on switching chronic hepatitis B patients to TAF highlighted its safety and efficacy, particularly in those with renal or bone concerns. (Aliment Pharmacol Ther, 2022) 7. Guidelines for the prevention, care, and treatment of chronic hepatitis B infection emphasize the importance of individualized treatment strategies to optimize patient outcomes. (WHO Guidelines) 8. A German multicenter study (GEMINIS) reported interim results showing the effectiveness of tenofovir in real-world practice for chronic hepatitis B over a two-year period. (J Hepatol, 2013) 9. A three-year study on TDF treatment for chronic hepatitis B demonstrated sustained efficacy and safety, with significant virological suppression and clinical benefits. (Gastroenterology, 2011) 10. Switching hepatitis B patients with kidney dysfunction from tenofovir to entecavir has been shown to improve renal outcomes while maintaining antiviral efficacy. (Liver Int, 2019) 11. A five-year open-label follow-up study revealed regression of cirrhosis in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with TDF, underscoring its long-term benefits. (Lancet, 2013) 12. A study comparing TDF, emtricitabine/TDF, and entecavir in patients with decompensated chronic hepatitis B liver disease highlighted the efficacy and safety of these antiviral regimens. (Hepatology, 2011) 13. Long-term therapy with tenofovir has been shown to be effective in patients co-infected with HIV and hepatitis B virus, with sustained virological suppression. (Gastroenterology, 2010) 14. Continuous entecavir therapy for three years in treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients resulted in viral suppression, low resistance rates, and favorable safety outcomes. (Am J Gastroenterol, 2011) 15. Long-term entecavir treatment has been associated with reduced incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B. (Hepatology, 2013) 16. A study on the use of entecavir in Japanese patients with chronic hepatitis B demonstrated its long-term safety and efficacy in nucleoside-naïve individuals. (J Hepatol, 2010) 17. Changes in HBsAg and HBV DNA levels after five years of entecavir treatment in Chinese chronic hepatitis B patients were documented, showing sustained virological control. (J Gastroenterol Hepatol, 2014) 18. The efficacy of entecavir, with or without TDF, in nucleos(t)ide-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients was confirmed in a multicenter study, demonstrating robust antiviral activity. (Gastroenterology, 2012) 19. A study on glomerular dysfunction in African patients receiving antiretroviral therapy highlighted the importance of monitoring renal function over time. (Antiviral Ther, 2011) 20. A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of TDF in adolescents with chronic hepatitis B demonstrated its efficacy and safety in this population. (Hepatology, 2012) 21. Pharmacokinetic data on TAF and tenofovir in African children receiving dolutegravir or boosted protease inhibitors provided insights into optimal dosing strategies. (Clin Infect Dis, 2023) 22. Bone mineral density among children living with HIV and failing first-line antiretroviral therapy in Uganda was assessed, emphasizing the need for monitoring bone health. (PLoS One, 2023) 23. A multicenter study in pregnant Chinese women with active chronic hepatitis B demonstrated the safety and efficacy of TAF in preventing perinatal HBV transmission. (Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol, 2021) 24. The use of TAF in early-to-middle pregnancy for mothers with chronic hepatitis B was shown to be safe and effective, with no significant adverse outcomes. (Front Med, 2022) 25. A national cohort study confirmed the efficacy and safety of TAF in preventing mother-to-child transmission of HBV, supporting its use in clinical practice. (Aliment Pharmacol Ther, 2020) 26. High rates of reversibility of renal damage were observed in HIV-infected patients receiving tenofovir-containing antiretroviral therapy, highlighting its renal safety profile. (Antiviral Res, 2012) 27. TAF has been shown to mitigate the effects of diabetes and body mass on serum alanine aminotransferase activities in chronic hepatitis B patients, suggesting metabolic benefits. (Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol, 2022) 28. Bone mineral density assessment in tenofovir-treated chronic hepatitis B patients identified fracture risk factors, emphasizing the importance of individualized risk assessment. (J Infect Dis, 2015) 29. Long-term entecavir therapy has been associated with histological improvement and reversal of fibrosis/cirrhosis in chronic hepatitis B patients. (Hepatology, 2010) 30. Long-term monitoring of HBV resistance to entecavir in nucleoside-naïve patients revealed that resistance remains rare over five years of therapy.
